the sensitivity of the 12-month retrospective recall of falls was 77.1%, and the specificity was 94.2%, with a positive predictive value (PPV) of 87.3% and a negative predictive value (NPV) of 85.7%.

1) the 12-month fall recall is a reasonable alternative method to ascertain falls in older women, 2) the sensitivity and specificity of the recall is comparable to the prospective ascertainment, and 3) the recall of falls can be improved by asking the women to recall falls over the previous year in a series of shorter recall intervals (3-month recall, 6-month recall, or 9-month recall).
